issue-canvaskit.md:
### Scope: hot restart versus state-preserving hot reload

State-preserving hot reload updates code in the running application and keeps its existing state. Hot restart runs `main()` again with fresh Dart application state while keeping the browser page. A full browser refresh creates a new page environment and is a different operation.

The accumulation and cadence measurements above are from **full hot restart** (`app.restart(fullRestart: true)`). The ordinary state-preserving hot-reload path retains the CanvasKit renderer and does not invoke the restart cleanup through `ext.flutter.disassemble`. We have not measured a state-preserving-hot-reload leak or performance improvement here.

PR #196786 registers renderer disposal for hot restart. Its surface resource-release code is also shared with ordinary surface disposal and offscreen canvas replacement, including resize-recovery paths. Consequently the PR is not exclusively restart-only code; that broader cleanup does not establish that the restart accumulation reported here also occurs on ordinary hot reload.

Source: [restart cleanup hook](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/22e676c57e1e6d04c2289a47368ea4093bbc3c18/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/initialization.dart#L149), [renderer registration](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3e25df705b11935d0a4a5750e6b8bc26460877b1/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/canvaskit/renderer.dart#L76), [shared surface release](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/3e25df705b11935d0a4a5750e6b8bc26460877b1/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/canvaskit/surface.dart#L269).
issue-listener.md:
### Scope: hot restart versus state-preserving hot reload

State-preserving hot reload updates code in the running application and keeps its existing state. Hot restart runs `main()` again with fresh Dart application state while keeping the browser page. A full browser refresh creates a new page environment and is a different operation.

The reproduction above is **full hot restart**, which disposes the outgoing web engine dispatcher through `ext.flutter.disassemble` and creates a new dispatcher. Ordinary state-preserving hot reload reuses the existing dispatcher, so it does not create the sequence of retired dispatchers measured here. A state-preserving-hot-reload retention leak has not been demonstrated by these measurements.

PR #196787 fixes `EnginePlatformDispatcher.dispose()` itself, so it also applies whenever that engine dispatcher is explicitly disposed outside restart. Disposing an application's `State` or rebuilding a widget is not the same as disposing the engine's dispatcher.

Source: [dispatcher restart registration and disposal](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/b8bbc80b12474d54da242a2e150c6fd6d8dbde9c/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/platform_dispatcher.dart#L37), [engine restart cleanup](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/22e676c57e1e6d04c2289a47368ea4093bbc3c18/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/initialization.dart#L149).
issue-ddc.md:
### Scope: hot restart versus state-preserving hot reload

State-preserving hot reload updates code in the running application and keeps its existing state. Hot restart runs `main()` again with fresh Dart application state while keeping the browser page. A full browser refresh creates a new page environment and is a different operation.

The measured native-metadata retention is from **canary DDC hot restart that replaces the runtime**. The new `disposeNativeExtensions()` calls in CL 578301 are in `LibraryManager.hotRestartEnd()` and its older `hotRestart()` API. Stateful `hotReloadEnd()` reuses existing library objects and does not invoke that disposal. Therefore these measurements establish runtime-replacement retention, not a state-preserving-hot-reload leak.

The stale-DOM-callback TypeError described below was also reproduced after **hot restart**, when the outgoing runtime's native method keys are removed. It has not been demonstrated for ordinary state-preserving hot reload. This distinction does not claim that every possible hot-reload memory or interop problem is absent.

Source: [DDC loader change and restart cleanup calls](https://dart-review.googlesource.com/c/sdk/+/578301/3/pkg/dev_compiler/lib/js/ddc/ddc_module_loader.js).
